rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Under the Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) rules, your employer may not employ you during the last six weeks before the birth, unless you expressly declare that you are willing to work. The statute's wording is "in den letzten sechs Wochen vor der Entbindung". You can withdraw such a declaration at any time for the future.

The six weeks are counted from the expected date of birth shown in the certificate from your doctor or midwife ("der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung ... wie er sich aus dem ärztlichen Zeugnis oder dem Zeugnis einer Hebamme ... ergibt"). If that certificate gives 15 November 2026, the six weeks before it begin in early October 2026: counting back 42 days from 15 November 2026 gives 4 October 2026. The excerpts do not set out a day-counting method, so your employer applies the exact start date.

If the baby is not born on the expected day, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match. After the birth, your employer may not employ you for eight weeks. This rises to twelve weeks for premature births, multiple births, and, if you apply for it, when a disability in the child is medically established within the first eight weeks. If the birth comes early, the period after the birth is extended by the days lost before it.

This protection applies to employment. The Familienportal states that self-employed women are not covered by the Mutterschutzgesetz.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law does not set an application deadline for Elterngeld (parental allowance). Instead, it limits how far back payment goes. Elterngeld must be applied for in writing, and it is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received: "Es wird rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats geleistet, in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist." Months of the child's life earlier than those three are not paid.

Elterngeld can be received from the day of birth. Basic Elterngeld can be received until the child completes the 14th month of life. Elterngeld Plus can run until the child completes the 32nd month of life, as long as at least one parent takes it in consecutive months from the 15th month onwards.

Which months are paid in your case, and how much, is decided by your Elterngeld office (Elterngeldstelle), which handles applications.
